headline: Learned models map metabolic sites and MS/MS annotations at atom and peak level
label: Learned Metabolite Identification Models
summary: Recent preprints tie learned representations to atom- and peak-level evidence to resolve metabolite-level questions with interpretable local correspondences.
synthesis: The metabolite-focused items share a preference for local, fine-grained correspondence over global scoring. ATTNSOM predicts atom-level sites of metabolism for cytochrome P450 isoforms using a shared graph encoder with cross-isoform attention. FLARE applies contrastive peak-node alignment to MS/MS metabolite annotation, reaching 43.15% rank@1 on MassSpecGym with interpretable local spectra-molecule correspondences. The remaining items apply comparable learned frameworks to protein, pathology, proteomic, knowledge-graph, and drug-association data without addressing metabolite identification directly. What is distinct in this set is the explicit linking of learned representations to atom- and peak-level evidence, with isoform-specific and spectral context treated as explicit modelling dimensions.
